chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and al-Razzaz from Ayoub ibn Nuh and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, all of them from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

Regarding a man who divorces his wife while he is sick, he said: If he dies in his illness and she has not remarried, she inherits him; and if she has remarried, then she has accepted what was done, there is no inheritance for her.
ai.seo_question: Does a wife inherit if her husband divorces her while sick and then dies?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of a wife in cases of 'divorce during illness' (talaq al-marid), a critical scenario in Shia jurisprudence where the husband's death might otherwise be presumed to result from the illness that triggered the divorce. The ruling hinges on the wife's subsequent marital status: remaining unmarried preserves her inheritance rights, while remarriage is interpreted as final acceptance of the divorce, thereby severing the inheritance link. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the wife's agency and the definitive nature of the divorce act even if the husband's death occurs shortly thereafter.
